latestRelease.publishedChanges: Network and replication improvements for multiplayer, especially large saves

versionBoundary: All available current production datasets agree. The SatisfactoryTools version index groups 1.2.3.1, 1.2.4.1 and 1.2.5.0. SCIM does not declare an exact patch. Original Docs was verified as 1.2.3.1. No separately obtained original 1.2.5.1 Docs was compared; latest release notes announce no recipe changes

method.comparison: Independent normalization, separate from the project refresh script; producers enumerated from each source
method.rates: Per minute at 100% clock; source litres converted to cubic metres for SCIM and original Docs. SatisfactoryTools already supplies fluid amounts in cubic metres
method.power: Original native building class determines fixed versus variable power. SatisfactoryTools uses variablePowerDraw only when building powerUsage is zero

uranium.name: Uranium Ore (Bauxite)
uranium.unlock: Tier 9 Matter Conversion milestone; background schematic Schematic_9-1-1_C, unlocked by Schematic_9-1_C
uranium.defaultPolicyReason: This is a real late-game milestone recipe, independent of hard-drive alternates. Scarcity weighting can prefer it over direct uranium extraction. Conversion therefore requires an explicit setting; importing hard-drive unlocks alone does not establish Tier 9 progression

scopeNotes: All 291 real manufacturing recipes are included; construction, hand-only crafting and generator fuel burning are outside the manufacturing scope
Normal SatisfactoryTools Stable has 276 manufacturing recipes; its FICSMAS variant adds the same 15 seasonal manufacturing recipes present in Factory Lens

SatisfactoryTools additionally synthesizes Fake_Recipe_Gift_C for the FICSMAS Gift Tree (15 gifts/min, 0 MW). Factory Lens models gifts as an external supply with a default limit of zero and does not count Gift Trees
Unused variable-power fields on Singularity Cell, Biochemical Sculptor and Ballistic Warp Drive do not override their fixed-power buildings; correct values are 55, 75 and 55 MW
